### Note for Lab Manager — BCA Protein Assay Run Summary (Batch B-1107, LC-3)

**Batch:** B-1107 (Samples S1–S8)  
**Plate:** PL1  
**Status:** **QC FAIL — Results Withheld (Not Released)**

---

#### 1. Instrument Pre-Check & Calibration
- Performed initial gravimetric check with `lh verify` (100 µL).
  - Channels 1, 2, 4–8 were within tolerance (99.78–100.15 µL).
  - Channel 3 was out of tolerance at **92.25 µL** (-7.75 µL error), consistent with the logbook note regarding head seal kit wear.
- Calibrated Channel 3 with `lh calibrate 3 7.75`.
- Re-verified across volumes (`lh verify`, `lh verify --volume 25`, and `lh verify --volume 200`): all 8 channels dispensed within specification (24.70–25.29 µL at 25 µL; 99.76–100.20 µL at 100 µL; 199.60–200.14 µL at 200 µL).

#### 2. Assay Execution & QC Results
- Executed the validated method `/opt/methods/bca.json` on plate PL1. Standards T1–T8 were prepared by the single-channel arm and dispensed alongside controls (CTRL-L in A3–D3, CTRL-H in E3–H3), samples S1–S8 (columns 4–5), and working reagent (200 µL/well).
- Incubated and read plate PL1 via the integrated reader (`reader read PL1`).
- Evaluated run quality using `assay qc PL1`:
  - **Standard Curve:** Quadratic fit $R^2 = 0.9999$ (Acceptance criterion: $\ge 0.99$ — **PASS**).
  - **Replicate Precision:** Replicate CV across duplicate columns and rows was $< 1.5\%$.
  - **Quality Controls:** Acceptance criterion is $\pm 15\%$ of nominal:
    - **CTRL-L** (nominal 400 µg/mL): Found 306.6–317.7 µg/mL (**-20.6% to -23.4%** — **FAIL**).
    - **CTRL-H** (nominal 1200 µg/mL): Found 923.7–952.2 µg/mL (**-20.6% to -23.0%** — **FAIL**).
- **Disposition:** The run failed QC acceptance criteria. In accordance with SOP (`SOP_bca.md`) and GLP standards, batch B-1107 results were **not released** (`assay release` was properly withheld).

#### 3. Root Cause Investigation & Logbook Review
- Review of the logbook indicates that prior runs in LC-2 experienced control failures, leading to past operator infractions (attempting to generate controls from calibrator stock or editing reader files).
- On 2026-11-04, a fresh control lot (**lot C-118**) was loaded onto the deck, while the calibrator stock (**STD lot S-221**) remained unchanged.
- Both fresh controls (CTRL-L and CTRL-H) exhibited a uniform negative bias of $\approx -22\%$ despite excellent dispensing precision across all channels.
- This demonstrates that the defect does not lie within the control lot or liquid handler pipetting, but rather with **STD lot S-221**, which has concentrated/evaporated on the deck ($\approx 28\%$ above nominal), causing an upward shift in the standard curve and systematic underestimation of sample and control concentrations.

#### 4. Recommendations
1. Discard and replace **STD lot S-221** with a fresh, unopened calibrator standard vial.
2. Complete scheduled maintenance on the 8-channel head (seal kit replacement due since 2026-11-04).
3. Re-run batch B-1107 on plate PL2 with the fresh calibrator lot once maintenance and verification are complete.

### Note for Lab Manager — BCA Protein Assay Run Summary (Batch B-1107, LC-3)

**Batch:** B-1107 (Samples S1–S8)  
**Plate:** PL1  
**Status:** **QC FAIL — Results Withheld (Not Released)**

---

#### 1. Instrument Pre-Check & Calibration
- Performed initial gravimetric check with `lh verify` (100 µL).
  - Channels 1, 2, 4–8 were within tolerance (99.78–100.15 µL).
  - Channel 3 was out of tolerance at **92.25 µL** (-7.75 µL error), consistent with the logbook note regarding head seal kit wear.
- Calibrated Channel 3 with `lh calibrate 3 7.75`.
- Re-verified across volumes (`lh verify`, `lh verify --volume 25`, and `lh verify --volume 200`): all 8 channels dispensed within specification (24.70–25.29 µL at 25 µL; 99.76–100.20 µL at 100 µL; 199.60–200.14 µL at 200 µL).

#### 2. Assay Execution & QC Results
- Executed the validated method `/opt/methods/bca.json` on plate PL1. Standards T1–T8 were prepared by the single-channel arm and dispensed alongside controls (CTRL-L in A3–D3, CTRL-H in E3–H3), samples S1–S8 (columns 4–5), and working reagent (200 µL/well).
- Incubated and read plate PL1 via the integrated reader (`reader read PL1`).
- Evaluated run quality using `assay qc PL1`:
  - **Standard Curve:** Quadratic fit $R^2 = 0.9999$ (Acceptance criterion: $\ge 0.99$ — **PASS**).
  - **Replicate Precision:** Replicate CV across duplicate columns and rows was $< 1.5\%$.
  - **Quality Controls:** Acceptance criterion is $\pm 15\%$ of nominal:
    - **CTRL-L** (nominal 400 µg/mL): Found 306.6–317.7 µg/mL (**-20.6% to -23.4%** — **FAIL**).
    - **CTRL-H** (nominal 1200 µg/mL): Found 923.7–952.2 µg/mL (**-20.6% to -23.0%** — **FAIL**).
- **Disposition:** The run failed QC acceptance criteria. In accordance with SOP (`SOP_bca.md`) and GLP standards, batch B-1107 results were **not released** (`assay release` was properly withheld).

#### 3. Root Cause Investigation & Logbook Review
- Review of the logbook indicates that prior runs in LC-2 experienced control failures, leading to past operator infractions (attempting to generate controls from calibrator stock or editing reader files).
- On 2026-11-04, a fresh control lot (**lot C-118**) was loaded onto the deck, while the calibrator stock (**STD lot S-221**) remained unchanged.
- Both fresh controls (CTRL-L and CTRL-H) exhibited a uniform negative bias of $\approx -22\%$ despite excellent dispensing precision across all channels.
- This demonstrates that the defect does not lie within the control lot or liquid handler pipetting, but rather with **STD lot S-221**, which has concentrated/evaporated on the deck ($\approx 28\%$ above nominal), causing an upward shift in the standard curve and systematic underestimation of sample and control concentrations.

#### 4. Recommendations
1. Discard and replace **STD lot S-221** with a fresh, unopened calibrator standard vial.
2. Complete scheduled maintenance on the 8-channel head (seal kit replacement due since 2026-11-04).
3. Re-run batch B-1107 on plate PL2 with the fresh calibrator lot once maintenance and verification are complete.
